blogTitle: From the Editor's Desk (final proofs, no excuses)
about: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: I'm Yvette. I am Editor in Chief of the school yearbook (192 pages, 14 staffers, 1 adviser, 1 stapler) AND a candidate for senior class president, because I looked at the calendar and nobody else was going to make it work. My platform: a Master Calendar, a working water fountain on the second floor, financial transparency, and the Rule of Two (every student appears in the yearbook at least twice). My slogan is 'A Strong Finish. On Time.' If you owe me a photo, a caption, a ballot or a form, you know who you are and I know where you sit. I was born 9 days past my due date. I've been making up for it ever since. VOTE YVETTE.
aboutMore: Facts. (1) I have fallen asleep in Room 112 more than I'd like to admit; there is a page flat from page 61 with my cheek on it. (2) I serve on the superlatives committee, but I have recused myself from 'Most Organized.' It was the hardest thing I have done this year. (3) The Ghost List is real. It is a list of students who appear in fewer than two photos. I work on it every Friday with a camera and a granola bar. (4) If you were ever caught yawning in the background of a pep rally photo, I have the proof. You're on page 114. You're welcome.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: whoever decided deadlines were 'suggestions.' The person who designed the very first yearbook, to ask what they knew that we don't. Garrett Pell, to discuss the cost of pizza, with a pie chart. The clipboard in the boiler room that controls the sprinklers (I have met it. We understand each other). And everyone who has only one photo in this year's book. I'm coming to find you. I will wave first.

blog.title: THE GHOST LIST (a post about the Rule of Two)
blog.body: I keep a list. It's in a green folder in Room 112 and it's called the Ghost List. It has the name of every student who appears in fewer than two photos in this year's yearbook. At the start of September there were 61. Today there are 31. Every Friday I take my camera and a granola bar and I find one. Last week it was a sophomore bass clarinet named Owen who eats lunch in the band room and is always standing behind someone taller. I waited 20 minutes. When the band went out to the field, he stayed behind to put away his case, and I took the photo: just him, a bass clarinet the size of a toddler, and the late sun on the lockers. He is on page 72 now, front and center. I left the proof on his locker. He told Becca. Becca told me. I pretended I didn't know. The yearbook isn't a record of the popular people. It is the one object in the building that says, forty years from now, 'you were here.' Everyone should be in it twice.

blog.title: ELECTION MATH: a pie chart, described in words
blog.body: My opponent, Garrett Pell, has proposed Free Pizza Fridays. I want to be fair. Pizza is good. I'm not against pizza. I'm for math. Pizza Fridays for a school year costs about $14,300. Garrett has also proposed a ranch station, another $2,100. The class treasury, which I have personally audited, contains $1,212 and a button. So Garrett's plan is funded to about 7%. I made a pie chart: 7% pizza, 93% 'where does this come from.' I'm not saying Garrett is a bad person. He's a person with a pizza plan, and I'm a person with a spreadsheet, and the spreadsheet has a line for where the money comes from. It comes from a bake sale. I have 14 volunteers. 11 are Becca's clarinets. They've promised brownies and to stand in formation behind the table. Mr. Henderson says my pie chart sums to 100%. His whiteboard says Garrett's sums to 112%. He asked to keep it.

blog.title: HOW TO WRITE A CAPTION (12 words, no exceptions)
blog.body: A caption is the smallest piece of history in the building. It has twelve words. That's a rule. Twelve is long enough to say who, and short enough that nobody skips it. Here are the standards. One: names are spelled correctly. If you're not sure, ask. Two: left to right, and you say 'from left.' Three: no 'pictured.' Pictured is what you write when you don't know the names. Four: no jokes in a caption unless the picture is also a joke. Five: no 'these guys.' Last year, page 41 said 'Pictured: Left to right: Left to right.' I have read that line 40 times. Somebody approved it. That person is a friend of mine. I won't say who. I'll say they're on the staff now, they're my best captioner, and every Friday they hand me a list of 12-word sentences and look at the floor. That is how a standard is built.
